np_hard_problems.complexity: NP-hard; APX-hard in the 1-gap case (no PTAS unless P=NP)
current_approaches: Integer Linear Programming (ILP) formulations (Aldy 4)
Semidefinite Programming (SDP) relaxations (Kalpakis & Namjoshi 2005)
Statistical phasing with reference panels (Beagle, Stargazer)
Combinatorial optimization with copy number and SV detection
gaps: No polynomial-time approximation scheme exists

Rare allele combinations (<0.1% frequency) remain difficult to phase accurately

np_hard_problems.problem: CYP2D6 Structural Variation and Copy Number Calling
np_hard_problems.complexity: NP-hard (ILP solving restricted to pharmacogene models)
current_approaches: Aldy 4: ILP-based combinatorial optimization for CNV and SV detection
Stargazer: paralog-specific copy number from read depths
Cyrius: SV-aware haplotyping (99.3% concordance vs Aldy 82-87%)
Long-read sequencing (PacBio, Oxford Nanopore) for direct phasing
gaps: Short-read NGS cannot resolve hybrid gene-pseudogene rearrangements
No tool achieves >99% concordance across all structural variant types
Reference panels lack diversity for non-European structural alleles

np_hard_problems.problem: Pharmacogenomic Variant Combination Optimization for Clinical Reporting

current_approaches: PharmCAT Named Allele Matcher: permutation-based matching with CPIC allele definitions

gaps: Combinatorial explosion as gene-drug pairs grow (34 genes, 164 drugs in CPIC)
Novel variants not in allele definitions are not considered
Multi-gene interactions (e.g., TPMT+NUDT15 compound metabolizer status) require heuristic approaches

bottlenecks.description: Battery life is the primary constraint for continuous multimodal monitoring. A wearable with a 300 mWh battery can support individual sensors for hundreds of hours, but combining ECG (1-5 mW), PPG (4-10 mW), EMG (6-15 mW), and IMU (0.3-1 mW) reduces runtime to under 10 hours. On-device ML inference can drain the battery in under an hour, making continuous monitoring incompatible with current energy budgets.
bottlenecks.evidence: AMI framework paper (arxiv.org/html/2604.10404v1): 'combining them reduces runtime to under 10 hours'; 'multimodal sensing combined with continuous on-device ML inference can drain a wearable battery in under an hour'

bottlenecks.description: Motion artifacts in PPG and ECG signals remain a fundamental signal processing challenge. Despite adaptive filtering, ICA, CycleGAN-based approaches, and multi-wavelength PPG systems, satisfactory removal of motion artifacts has not been achieved. Beat-detection errors persist even in low-motion data, implying artifact removal alone does not guarantee accurate inter-beat interval and pulse rate variability estimation.
bottlenecks.evidence: Watanabe et al. 2025 (dl.acm.org/doi/abs/10.1145/3714394.3756241): 'sizeable beat-detection errors even in low-motion data'; Poh M.-Z. et al. (PMC7085621): 'satisfactory performance in removing or reducing motion artifacts has not yet been achieved'

bottlenecks.description: Patient adherence to wearable devices is a major obstacle in remote monitoring. In a pilot cohort of older adults, while daily adherence was high (median 92.1%), 32% of participants wore the device fewer than 4 days within a 14-day period. Compliance is multifactorial, influenced by age, symptom severity, environmental factors, and device usability.
bottlenecks.evidence: Ding et al. 2024 (pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39454101): '32% (7/22) of participants exhibited lower adherence, with the device worn on fewer than 4 days within the requested initial 14-day period'; WEAICOR study (PMC10131852): 'compliance to wearables was a major challenge'

bottlenecks.description: Consumer sleep trackers show poor accuracy for sleep staging compared to polysomnography. Mean absolute percent errors for deep sleep and REM sleep were all above 20% across devices. Proportional bias patterns are prevalent: devices overestimate shorter sleep stages and underestimate longer ones. No consumer device can replace PSG for clinical sleep assessment.
bottlenecks.evidence: Kainec et al. 2024 (Sensors, doi:10.3390/s24020635): 'mean absolute percent errors for deep sleep and REM sleep were all above 20%'; 'proportional bias patterns in consumer sleep-tracking technologies are prevalent'

bottlenecks.description: Interoperability between wearable devices and healthcare information systems remains limited. Heterogeneous communication protocols (BLE, Wi-Fi, Zigbee, LoRa, NB-IoT, 5G) and proprietary platforms complicate data exchange. Less than 8% of wearable health data ever leaves the manufacturer's proprietary ecosystem, creating structural barriers to clinical integration.
bottlenecks.evidence: Majumder et al. 2017 (doi.org/10.1007/s12553-023-00801-y): 'heterogeneous communication protocols and proprietary platforms complicate interoperability'; Comcast P2P BoR proposal (thegadgetdigest.com): 'less than 8% of this data ever leaves the manufacturer's proprietary ecosystem'

bottlenecks.description: Data transmission reliability across wireless protocols presents tradeoffs. BLE cannot support higher data rates or long-distance communication. LoRaWAN offers long range but limited payload constraints. NB-IoT provides wide-area coverage but higher deployment costs. Latency exceeding 1.2 seconds causes misalignment between ECG and motion artifacts, compromising clinical algorithms.
bottlenecks.evidence: Uddin & Koo 2024 (doi.org/10.1016/j.iot.2024.101124): 'BLE technology cannot be used for higher data rates and long-distance wireless communications'; Telematic wearables analysis (thegadgetdigest.com): 'delays exceeding 1.2 seconds cause misalignment between ECG and motion artifacts'

np_hard_problems.problem: Molecular Docking (Maximum Weighted Independent Set / Maximum Vertex-Weighted Clique)
np_hard_problems.complexity: NP-hard — mapping pharmacophore interactions to graph vertices and finding the optimal compatible subset is provably intractable for large densely connected graphs
current_approaches: Force-field-based stochastic search (AutoDock Vina, Glide SP)
Graph-based combinatorial optimization mapping to MWIS/MVWCP
Quantum annealing on neutral-atom QPUs (Rydberg blockade)
Deep learning pose prediction (diffusion models, regression architectures)
Hybrid physics-ML frameworks (RosettaVS, TerraBind)
gaps: Size mismatch between biologically relevant systems and NISQ quantum hardware capacity
Heuristic search provides no optimality guarantees
Scoring functions lack accuracy for entropy and induced-fit effects
DL methods show poor generalization to novel binding pockets

np_hard_problems.problem: Protein Sidechain Packing (Rotamer Assignment)
np_hard_problems.complexity: NP-hard — selecting one rotamer per residue from a discrete library to minimize total pairwise-decomposable conformational energy is provably intractable (Pierce & Winfree, 2002)
current_approaches: Dead-end elimination (DEE)
Integer linear programming
Monte Carlo stochastic search (Rosetta packer)
Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA) with QUBO encoding
AlphaFold2 backbone prediction + refinement
gaps: AlphaFold2 sidechain positioning deviates from experimental data by up to 20%
Rosetta packer is heuristic with no global optimality guarantee
QAOA shot scaling remains below classical exhaustive search rates at moderate flexibility
Classical preprocessing does not significantly reduce low-energy basins

np_hard_problems.problem: Protein Structure Alignment (Optimal RMSD under Correspondence)
np_hard_problems.complexity: NP-hard — reducible to the largest common point set (LCP) problem or 3D substructure isomorphism, both proven NP-complete (Goldman et al., 1999)
current_approaches: Dynamic programming (CE, Dali)
Spectral methods (GESAMT)
Heuristic search (TM-align)
Contact map overlap maximization
gaps: Exhaustive search is O(n!·m!) for proteins of length n, m
Continuous 6-DOF search space cannot be discretely sampled without missing global optimum
Scoring functions are non-convex with many local minima
Flexible alignment with rotamers is NP-complete to NP-hard

np_hard_problems.problem: Protein Threading (3D Fold Recognition)
np_hard_problems.complexity: NP-complete for detailed models (Lathrop, 1994) — aligning sequence to structural template with pairwise interactions is intractable
current_approaches: Dynamic programming over frozen environments
Graph-based algorithms
Deep learning fold recognition
gaps: Simplified models required for tractability
Energy function accuracy degrades with sequence length
Cannot guarantee optimal fold assignment

np_hard_problems.problem: Flexible Ligand-Flexible Receptor Docking
np_hard_problems.complexity: NP-hard — even simplified models with both ligand and receptor flexibility are intractable (Fraenkel, 1993)
current_approaches: FFT correlation methods
Monte Carlo simulation
Genetic algorithms
Incremental construction (DOCK, FlexX)
gaps: Induced-fit effects poorly captured by rigid-receptor approximations
Ensemble docking multiplies computational cost
No polynomial-time algorithm exists for guaranteed optimal solution

np_hard_problems.problem: Multi-Resource Constrained Elective Surgical Scheduling (MESS)

current_approaches: Nash equilibrium-based game-theoretic allocation across three player types
Digital twin-based simulation for surgical scheduling optimization
Meta-heuristic algorithms for multi-objective optimization (APT, AOT, TC)

Nash equilibrium computation is PPAD-complete in general games
Integration with real-time IoT device availability data remains unsolved

Device-assisted computation offloading with idle resource differentiation
Heuristic partitioning with greedy result allocation

bottlenecks.description: Eligibility criteria are written in free-text natural language with complex nested logic (AND/OR/NOT), temporal constraints, and numeric thresholds, making automated parsing and matching extremely difficult. bottlenecks.description: EHR data heterogeneity across institutions creates a semantic interoperability gap: eligibility criteria must be mapped to institution-specific schemas (OMOP, i2b2, Epic), and 80% of clinically relevant information resides in unstructured notes

np_hard_problems.problem: Minimum-Cost Set Cover for Clinical Trial Site Selection: Selecting the minimum-cost set of investigative sites that collectively cover all required patient subpopulations, geographic regions, and enrollment targets. This is a generalization of the NP-hard Set Cover problem (Karp 1972).
np_hard_problems.complexity: NP-hard; greedy approximation achieves H(n) ≈ ln(n)+1 ratio, which is optimal unless P=NP (Feige 1998)
current_approaches: Greedy set cover heuristics with cost-effectiveness scoring
Integer linear programming (ILP) for exact solutions on small instances
Genetic algorithms for multi-objective optimization (accuracy, fairness, competition)
DocTr: cross-modal deep learning with genetic algorithm optimization for clinician-trial matching (Gao et al. 2026, Nature Health)
gaps: No polynomial-time algorithm can beat ln(n) approximation unless P=NP
Multi-objective fairness constraints (racial, ethnic, geographic diversity) make the problem harder
Dynamic enrollment rates and site capacity constraints are not well-modeled

np_hard_problems.problem: Patient-Trial Matching as Bipartite Graph Assignment: Matching patients to trials where each patient may be eligible for multiple trials and each trial has multiple slots, with the objective of maximizing total enrollment while respecting eligibility constraints. This is a generalization of the Assignment Problem with additional constraints.
np_hard_problems.complexity: NP-hard when extended to many-to-many matching with eligibility constraints; basic assignment is polynomial (Hungarian algorithm O(n³)) but constrained versions are NP-hard
current_approaches: DeepEnroll: cross-modal deep embedding with entailment prediction (Zhang et al. 2020)
TrialGPT: LLM-based matching with criterion-level evaluation (Jin et al. 2024, Nature Communications)
COMPOSE: embedding-based patient-trial matching (Gao et al. 2020)
TrialMatchAI: RAG-based hybrid search with criterion-level eligibility assessment (Abdallah et al. 2025)
SMT-based matching: Satisfiability Modulo Theories for logical reasoning over eligibility criteria (Stanford LAM)
gaps: O(n²) pairwise matching complexity does not scale to millions of patients × 500K trials
LLM-based approaches struggle with temporal logic, derived clinical variables, and numeric thresholds
Generalizability across disease areas and institutions remains limited
No approach guarantees 100% recall with high precision at scale

np_hard_problems.problem: Set Balancing for Stratified Randomization: Partitioning patients into treatment arms such that all arms have nearly identical distributions of covariates (age, sex, biomarkers, disease severity) while differing only in treatment assignment. This is the NP-hard Set Balancing problem.
np_hard_problems.complexity: NP-hard; no known polynomial-time exact algorithm; approximation algorithms and heuristics required
current_approaches: Stratified permuted block randomization
Minimization methods (Pocock & Simon)
Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA) and Quantum Walk Optimization (QWOA) for QUBO formulations (arXiv:2509.07200)
Shannon-entropy-based post-processing for feature-distribution uniformity
gaps: High-dimensional covariate spaces make exact balancing infeasible
No constant-factor approximation known for general case
Dynamic/adaptive balancing during trial enrollment adds further complexity

np_hard_problems.problem: Combinatorial Optimization for Eligibility Criteria Design: Selecting the optimal set of eligibility criteria that maximizes eligible patient pool while maintaining scientific validity and statistical power. Each criterion eliminates a multiplicative fraction of candidates.
np_hard_problems.complexity: NP-hard; equivalent to a constrained optimization over combinatorial space of criteria combinations
current_approaches: NLP-based simulation of eligible patient counts under different criteria combinations (Sharma et al. 2024, JMIR)
Knowledge-base-driven criteria optimization using real-world EHR data
FDA 2022 guidance on eligibility broadening
gaps: Criteria interactions are multiplicative and non-linear, making optimization difficult
Trade-off between internal validity (strict criteria) and external validity (broad criteria) is not formally optimized
Rare disease trials face extreme combinatorial explosion of biomarker combinations

sota_approaches.name: TrialGPT

sota_approaches.name: DeepEnroll

sota_approaches.citation: Zhang et al. 2020, arXiv:2001.08179

sota_approaches.name: Syntax (Adaptive Experiment Design with Synthetic Controls)
sota_approaches.description: Trial design that adaptively recruits patients to identify subpopulations with positive treatment effect, using synthetic controls that combine control samples from other subpopulations. Sample-efficient via thresholding bandit principles.
sota_approaches.citation: Hüyük, Qian, van der Schaar 2024, AISTATS 2024, PMLR 238:1180-1188

sota_approaches.name: BASIC (Bayesian Adaptive Synthetic-Control Design)

sota_approaches.citation: Jiang et al. 2023, Clinical Trials, doi:10.1177/17407745231176445

sota_approaches.name: SECRETS (Subject-Efficient Clinical RCTs using Synthetic Intervention)
sota_approaches.description: Framework that increases RCT power by simulating cross-over design using synthetic intervention to estimate individual treatment effects. Reduces required subjects by 10-3,957 per arm while maintaining 80% power.

sota_approaches.name: TrialMatchAI
sota_approaches.description: End-to-end AI-powered recommendation system using fine-tuned open-source LLMs with RAG framework. sota_approaches.citation: Abdallah et al. 2025, arXiv:2505.08508

sota_approaches.name: EC2Seq2Sql

sota_approaches.name: DocTr
sota_approaches.description: Cross-modal deep learning framework for matching clinicians with clinical trials, integrating NLP, graph-based learning, and fairness-aware optimization via genetic algorithms.
sota_approaches.citation: Gao et al. 2026, Nature Health, doi:10.1038/s44360-026-00073-6

sota_approaches.name: RFAN (Randomize First Augment Next)

sota_approaches.citation: Klein et al. 2025, AISTATS 2025, PMLR 258

sota_approaches.name: SMT-Based Clinical Trial Matching

failure_modes.mode: LLM hallucination in eligibility criteria parsing: LLMs may generate plausible but incorrect eligibility assessments, particularly for temporal logic, derived clinical variables (eGFR, QTc), and numeric thresholds
failure_modes.mitigation: Human-in-the-loop review with criterion-level verification; structured EHR queries for numeric thresholds; temporal rule engines; confidence scoring with escalation

failure_modes.mode: Temporal logic errors: Criteria involving 'within 6 months of diagnosis' or 'no prior therapy in past 12 months' require precise event ordering and interval calculation that LLMs frequently get wrong
failure_modes.mitigation: Dedicated temporal rule engines; computable phenotype logic; explicit date anchoring to diagnosis/screening dates

failure_modes.mode: Data quality and missingness: EHR data may be incomplete, coded differently across institutions, or missing key eligibility-determining information, leading to false positives and false negatives
failure_modes.mitigation: Multi-source data fusion; missingness-aware matching with explicit uncertainty quantification; institution-specific ontology mapping

failure_modes.mode: Interoperability failure in DCT platforms: Fragmented vendor systems create data silos, redundant transcription, and audit trail gaps that compromise regulatory compliance
failure_modes.mitigation: Hub-and-spoke architecture with centralized integration layer; adoption of FHIR/OMOP standards; risk-based validation of each integration point

failure_modes.mode: Synthetic control arm bias: Historical control data may not be comparable to trial patients due to differences in standard of care, patient selection, or data collection methods
failure_modes.mitigation: BASIC design with adaptive switching to RCT; propensity score matching with comparability thresholds; sensitivity analysis for unmeasured confounding

failure_modes.mode: Algorithmic bias in patient matching: Models trained on non-representative data may systematically exclude minority populations, exacerbating health disparities
failure_modes.mitigation: Fairness-aware optimization (DocTr genetic algorithm); diverse training data; demographic parity constraints; regular bias audits

failure_modes.mode: Regulatory non-compliance: AI-generated eligibility decisions may lack the audit trails, explainability, and validation documentation required by FDA 21 CFR Part 11 and GCP
failure_modes.mitigation: Comprehensive audit logging of all AI outputs; validated AI/ML SaMD frameworks; CONSORT-AI/SPIRIT-AI reporting compliance

np_hard_problems.problem: Multipartite entity resolution (patient record linkage across multiple databases)
np_hard_problems.complexity: NP-hard — formulated as the Multidimensional Assignment Problem (MAP); brute-force comparison is O(n²) requiring (n²-n)/2 comparisons
current_approaches: Blocking techniques (sorted neighborhood, bigram indexing, canopy generation) to reduce comparison space from O(n²) to O(n·b)
Fellegi-Sunter probabilistic model with EM algorithm for weight computation
Greedy and Very Large Scale Neighborhood Search (VLNS) heuristics for MAP
Hybrid contrastive learning + deterministic rules with clique cover clustering
Bloom filter-based privacy-preserving record linkage
gaps: No polynomial-time exact solution exists for multipartite case
Optimal clique cover is NP-hard; greedy heuristics used in practice
Missing and erroneous QID values degrade linkage quality
Scalability beyond 300K records requires aggressive blocking that loses recall

np_hard_problems.problem: Ontology matching and semantic alignment between heterogeneous terminologies (SNOMED CT, ICD-10, LOINC, RxNorm, CPT, NDC)
np_hard_problems.complexity: NP-hard — correlation clustering formulation; subquadratic approximation required for practical use
current_approaches: Expert-curated reference sets for direct 1-to-1 mappings
Logistic regression-based imputation with medBERT text embeddings (AUC 0.95+ for NDC, 0.85 for CPT)
Patient-context-aware ranking using SNOMED CT hierarchical structure (Node2Vec, shortest-path, cosine similarity)
Two-step LLM-based alignment pipeline with candidate generation and acceptance/rejection
UMLS Metathesaurus as cross-terminology mapping backbone
gaps: Full automation remains an open problem requiring advances in ontology alignment and ML-driven entity resolution
Multiple regional versions of SNOMED CT and ICD-10 coexist with frequent updates
No gold standard mappings exist for CPT and NDC to SNOMED CT
Context-dependent mappings (one LOINC to multiple SNOMED CT codes) resist 1-to-1 automation

np_hard_problems.problem: Schema matching and data harmonization across heterogeneous EHR formats
np_hard_problems.complexity: NP-hard — correlation clustering is NP-hard (Filkov and Skiena 2003; Bansal et al. 2004); pairwise schema matching scales as O(N²) in number of schemas
current_approaches: Ontology-based mediation with vector-space embeddings for candidate generation
LLM-based accept/reject classification for candidate pairs
OMOP CDM as common target model with ETL transformation pipelines
FHIR StructureMap and ConceptMap for declarative transformations
AQL (Archetype Query Language) for openEHR-to-OMOP conversion via Eos/OMOCL
gaps: No universal automated harmonization solution exists
Institution-specific data collection standards and infrastructure differences persist
Medical knowledge evolves continuously making static mappings obsolete
Full interoperability requires advances in ontology alignment, ML-driven entity resolution, and expert validation simultaneously

np_hard_problems.problem: Optimal feature selection in high-dimensional omics data
np_hard_problems.complexity: NP-hard: search space includes 2^n - 1 feature subsets for n features; no polynomial-time algorithm achieves minimax-optimal recovery under worst-case designs
current_approaches: Filter methods (t-test, ANOVA, Wilcoxon, mutual information, MRMR)
Wrapper methods with metaheuristic optimization (SPHMO, genetic algorithms)
Embedded methods (LASSO, elastic net, tree-based importance)
Hybrid filter-plus-elimination (FLASH, MAFS with multi-head attention)
Quantum-inspired QUBO formulations for gene selection
gaps: No polynomial-time algorithm achieves information-theoretic optimal sample complexity
Heuristic methods yield inconsistent performance across datasets
Statistical-computational trade-off: efficient algorithms require stronger design conditions (restricted eigenvalues, incoherence)
Scalability limited to feature spaces of ~18,000 features in practice

np_hard_problems.problem: Best subset selection for multi-omics biomarker discovery
np_hard_problems.complexity: NP-hard: statistically minimax optimal but computationally intractable; exponential in the number of features
current_approaches: Convex relaxation (Lasso, sparse PCA)
Graphlet screening for sparse Gram matrices
AdaSub / local search with polynomial adaptivity
Two-stage ETS framework with polylog time per estimate
gaps: Efficient algorithms incur additional sample complexity cost inversely proportional to squared restricted eigenvalue
No method simultaneously achieves minimax statistical optimality and polynomial computational complexity
Multi-omics extension of best subset selection remains largely unexplored

np_hard_problems.problem: Network alignment and matching across omics layers
np_hard_problems.complexity: NP-hard: subgraph isomorphism and graph matching problems; exact alignment of multi-layer networks is computationally infeasible at scale
current_approaches: Graph-linked unified embedding (GLUE) with guidance graphs
Anchor-based integration (Seurat CCA/RPCA)
Manifold alignment (Pamona)
Non-negative matrix factorization (LIGER iNMF)
gaps: Scalable exact alignment remains elusive for atlas-scale datasets
Prior knowledge graphs may be incomplete or biased
Unpaired data integration requires approximate matching with quality guarantees

np_hard_problems.problem: Multi-objective optimization for omics layer selection and integration strategy
np_hard_problems.complexity: NP-hard: selecting optimal omics layers and integration architecture involves combinatorial optimization over 2^k possible layer combinations and multiple competing objectives
current_approaches: Unsupervised factor analysis (MOFA+) for automatic relevance determination
Supervised latent variable approaches (DIABLO)
Network-based integration with modularity optimization
gaps: No principled method for determining which omics layers to include a priori
Integration strategy selection (early/intermediate/late) remains largely heuristic
Trade-offs between interpretability and predictive performance not formally characterized

sota_approaches.name: MOFA+ (Multi-Omics Factor Analysis+)
sota_approaches.description: Bayesian group factor analysis framework for unsupervised integration of multi-modal single-cell data; decomposes variance into shared and view-specific factors; handles missing data natively via probabilistic framework; scales to ~100k cells

sota_approaches.name: Seurat WNN (Weighted Nearest Neighbor)

sota_approaches.name: GLUE (Graph-Linked Unified Embedding)
sota_approaches.description: Deep learning framework using variational graph autoencoders with prior knowledge guidance graphs to link omics-specific feature spaces; achieves sublinear computational scalability; first method to integrate millions of cells accurately

sota_approaches.name: LIGER (Integrative Non-negative Matrix Factorization)

np_hard_problems.problem: Nurse Rostering Problem (NRP) / Nurse Scheduling Problem (NSP)
np_hard_problems.complexity: NP-hard; proven strongly NP-hard even with only three work shifts and one day-off shift; exact solutions feasible only for small instances
current_approaches: Mixed Integer Linear Programming (MILP) with branch-and-price for small instances
Constraint Programming (CP-SAT) enforcing 14 hard constraints with 15 soft objectives

Multi-objective NSGA-II for Pareto-optimal trade-offs between cost, coverage, and satisfaction
gaps: Cannot guarantee regulatory compliance at scale
Lack real-time adaptability to staff shortages or emergency priorities
Multi-role, multi-skill workforce heterogeneity poorly modeled
Inter-week schedule stability and cross-midnight shift patterns remain challenging

np_hard_problems.problem: Medical Appointment Scheduling with Clinical Constraints

current_approaches: Answer Set Programming (ASP) for declarative constraint solving with <0.04s solve times

First-Come-First-Served (FCFS) and Random Choice as deterministic baselines
gaps: Centralized reservation systems (e.g., Italy's CUP) assign appointments without considering medical urgency, patient location, or preferences

Customized optimization techniques needed for each healthcare setting
Scalability to large patient populations remains limited

scalability_limits.threshold: Edge servers can become saturated under high traffic, preventing user requests from being completed; cloud fallback required when edge utilization exceeds 80%

GPU-accelerated cardiac twins require ~10^6 finite element nodes; real-time simulation at >30Hz requires >1 TFLOPS sustained compute per twin
Genotype-phenotype queries across >10M exomes require distributed Spark clusters with >100 nodes; query latency degrades from 3s to >30s beyond this scale without pre-aggregation
Single-agent clinical workflows expand from 25k to 3.9M tokens at 80-task batches; multi-agent partitioning reduces this 65-fold but orchestrator overhead increases at small batch sizes

top_np_hard_problems.problem: Single Individual SNP Haplotyping (SIH) / Minimum Error Correction (MEC)
top_np_hard_problems.complexity: NP-hard; APX-hard in the 1-gap case (no PTAS unless P=NP)
current_approaches: Integer Linear Programming (ILP) formulations (Aldy 4)
Semidefinite Programming (SDP) relaxations (Kalpakis & Namjoshi 2005)
Statistical phasing with reference panels (Beagle, Stargazer)
Combinatorial optimization with copy number and SV detection
gaps: No polynomial-time approximation scheme exists
Exact solutions scale exponentially with number of variants
Rare allele combinations (<0.1% frequency) remain difficult to phase accurately

top_np_hard_problems.problem: CYP2D6 Structural Variation and Copy Number Calling
top_np_hard_problems.complexity: NP-hard (ILP solving restricted to pharmacogene models)
current_approaches: Aldy 4: ILP-based combinatorial optimization for CNV and SV detection
Stargazer: paralog-specific copy number from read depths
Cyrius: SV-aware haplotyping (99.3% concordance vs Aldy 82-87%)
Long-read sequencing (PacBio, Oxford Nanopore) for direct phasing
gaps: Short-read NGS cannot resolve hybrid gene-pseudogene rearrangements
No tool achieves >99% concordance across all structural variant types
Reference panels lack diversity for non-European structural alleles

top_np_hard_problems.problem: Pharmacogenomic Variant Combination Optimization for Clinical Reporting
top_np_hard_problems.complexity: NP-hard (reducible to set cover / combinatorial matching)
current_approaches: PharmCAT Named Allele Matcher: permutation-based matching with CPIC allele definitions
Rule-based expert systems for guideline translation
FHIR Genomics + CDS Hooks for EHR-triggered reporting
gaps: Combinatorial explosion as gene-drug pairs grow (34 genes, 164 drugs in CPIC)
Novel variants not in allele definitions are not considered
Multi-gene interactions (e.g., TPMT+NUDT15 compound metabolizer status) require heuristic approaches

top_np_hard_problems.problem: Clinical pathway scheduling and resource allocation - optimizing patient flow through treatment activities with constrained resources (staff, equipment, beds)
top_np_hard_problems.complexity: NP-hard (reduction from job shop scheduling); strongly NP-hard for block scheduling variants
current_approaches: Hybrid genetic algorithms with particle swarm optimization
Timed continuous Petri nets (TCPNs) for pathway modeling
Stochastic process algebra (PEPA) for performance analysis
Mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) for radiotherapy scheduling
Column generation approaches for radiation therapy patient scheduling
gaps: Exact solutions computationally infeasible for real-world hospital scale
Stochastic patient arrival and service times not fully captured
Multi-objective optimization (patient wait time, resource utilization, clinical outcomes) remains challenging

top_np_hard_problems.problem: Optimal antibiotic treatment planning (Antibiotics Time Machine) - finding optimal sequence of antibiotics to minimize resistance
top_np_hard_problems.complexity: NP-hard (reduction from 3-SAT)
current_approaches: Markov decision process formulations
Exhaustive enumeration for small instances (up to 6 antibiotics)
Heuristic and metaheuristic search methods
gaps: No polynomial-time algorithm exists for general case
Combinatorial explosion with number of antibiotics and treatment length
Patient-specific factors (allergies, comorbidities) add dimensionality

top_np_hard_problems.problem: Drug combination optimization - selecting optimal subset of drugs maximizing synergy while minimizing adverse interactions
top_np_hard_problems.complexity: NP-hard (equivalent to maximum independent set / QUBO formulations)
current_approaches: Quadratic unconstrained binary optimization (QUBO)
Quantum annealing and quantum-inspired methods
Feedback system control (FSC) for iterative optimization
Two-step optimization: regimen selection then dose optimization
Literature data mining for candidate pre-selection
gaps: 20-50 drug libraries yield >60,000 possible regimens of 2-6 drugs
Dose-dependent interactions not captured by pairwise models
Clinical validation of computationally optimized combinations remains expensive

top_np_hard_problems.problem: K-adaptability in robust treatment planning - computing K treatment plans in advance for proton therapy under uncertainty
top_np_hard_problems.complexity: NP-hard (reduction from hitting set problem)
current_approaches: Two-phase heuristic: scenario clustering then plan redistribution
Mixed-integer programming for plan-scenario assignment
Min-max-min robust optimization formulations
gaps: Continuous-variable K-adaptability proven NP-hard
Clinical implementation requires real-time plan selection
Uncertainty sets grow exponentially with number of scenarios

top_np_hard_problems.problem: Optimal patch selection and tiling strategy for whole slide image analysis under memory constraints
top_np_hard_problems.complexity: NP-hard (reduces to maximum coverage problem with spatial constraints)
current_approaches: Two-stage patch-to-bag pipelines with frozen feature extractors
Multiple Instance Learning (MIL) with attention-based pooling
Pseudo-bag construction via Instance Sampling without Replacement (ISR) with KMeans clustering
Feature bridging and translation alignment (FBTA)
gaps: Frozen feature extractors create semantic gap with downstream classification objective
End-to-end backpropagation through tens of thousands of patches exceeds single-GPU memory
Tiling sacrifices spatial context critical for diagnosis

top_np_hard_problems.problem: Multi-objectivity optimization for segmentation architecture search (accuracy vs. computational cost vs. memory footprint)
top_np_hard_problems.complexity: NP-hard (multi-objective combinatorial optimization)
current_approaches: nnU-Net self-configuring framework with rule-based architecture selection
Auto3DSeg with SegResNet, DiNTS, SwinUNETR architectures
Neural architecture search (NAS) with hardware-aware constraints
gaps: Search space grows exponentially with number of objectives
Hardware-specific optima do not transfer across GPU generations
No guarantee of Pareto optimality in practice

top_np_hard_problems.problem: Feature selection and dimensionality reduction for radiomics-based classification
top_np_hard_problems.complexity: NP-hard (subset selection problem)
current_approaches: LASSO and elastic net regularization
Recursive feature elimination
Deep learning-based automatic feature extraction
gaps: High-dimensional feature spaces (thousands of radiomic features) with small sample sizes
Interpretability vs. performance tradeoff
Site-specific feature instability

top_np_hard_problems.problem: Optimal client selection and aggregation strategy for federated learning with non-IID data distributions
top_np_hard_problems.complexity: NP-hard (combinatorial optimization over client subsets)
current_approaches: FedAvg with uniform aggregation
FedProx with proximal regularization
Personalized federated learning (pFLSynth)
Domain-adversarial neural networks (DANN) with proximal regularization (FedDAPL)
gaps: Communication rounds scale with number of clients
Non-IID data causes client drift
Privacy-accuracy tradeoff with differential privacy

top_np_hard_problems.problem: Joint sensor selection and sampling-rate optimization for energy-constrained wearables (APSSE problem)
top_np_hard_problems.complexity: NP-hard (reducible to Integer Linear Programming; proven NP-hard in Appendix VIII of the Viveka paper)
current_approaches: Two-stage heuristic: first determine minimal sensor set per activity, then identify optimal sampling rate per sensor using Nyquist-Shannon theorem in energy-aware context
Greedy selection algorithms for sensor subset selection
Reinforcement learning agents for context-aware selective sensing and querying
Differentiable Gumbel-Sigmoid gating for dynamic sensor selection (AMI framework)
gaps: Exact solvers are intractable for real-time wearable deployment
Heuristics yield suboptimal solutions with no approximation guarantees
Joint optimization of sensing and inference remains disconnected in most prior works
Hardware-aware adaptation with dynamic computation graphs is still in early stages

top_np_hard_problems.problem: Optimal sensor scheduling for timely status updates in multi-source body sensor networks
top_np_hard_problems.complexity: NP-hard (scheduling for age minimization in wireless networks under physical interference constraints is NP-hard)
current_approaches: Maximum Age First (MAF) scheduler for optimal scheduling policy
Zero-wait sampler with semi-Markov decision process formulation
Dynamic programming for optimal sampler design
Sliding window and thresholding strategies for limited-computation sensor scheduling
gaps: Optimal scheduler-sampler pair requires solving SDP which is computationally expensive
Stationary deterministic sampler optimality only proven for specific network configurations
Multi-source networks with channel uncertainty remain intractable
Real-time implementation on resource-constrained wearables is unexplored

top_np_hard_problems.problem: Minimum Connected Dominating Set (MCDS) for wearable body sensor network topology optimization
top_np_hard_problems.complexity: NP-hard (MCDS is a classical NP-hard optimization problem; also related to Range Assignment and TDMA slot allocation which are NP-hard)
current_approaches: Metaheuristics and approximation algorithms for sensor deployment
Graph node partitioning based on sampling theory for graph signals
Difference-of-convex (DC) optimization for dynamic sensor scheduling
Greedy selection for graph signal sampling set selection
gaps: MCDS computation does not scale to large body sensor networks
Dynamic topology changes due to body movement are not well modeled
Energy-balanced dominating set construction remains heuristic
Joint optimization of coverage, connectivity, and energy is unsolved

top_np_hard_problems.problem: Optimal sensor deployment and coverage for body-worn sensor networks
top_np_hard_problems.complexity: NP-hard (variant of Art Gallery problem; deciding if k sensors suffice for triple coverage is NP-hard)
current_approaches: Art Gallery problem-based layout optimization
Connected Dominating Set (CDS) approximation
Weighted Set Cover (SCP) formulation for demand point coverage
Minimum Degree Spanning Tree (MDST) for energy-balanced deployment
gaps: Body-worn deployment adds anatomical constraints not captured by planar models
Sensor position optimization for signal quality is not well formulated
Multi-objective coverage (signal quality + connectivity + energy) is intractable
Personalized deployment based on body geometry is an open problem

top_np_hard_problems.problem: Molecular Docking (Maximum Weighted Independent Set / Maximum Vertex-Weighted Clique)
top_np_hard_problems.complexity: NP-hard — mapping pharmacophore interactions to graph vertices and finding the optimal compatible subset is provably intractable for large densely connected graphs
current_approaches: Force-field-based stochastic search (AutoDock Vina, Glide SP)
Graph-based combinatorial optimization mapping to MWIS/MVWCP
Quantum annealing on neutral-atom QPUs (Rydberg blockade)
Deep learning pose prediction (diffusion models, regression architectures)
Hybrid physics-ML frameworks (RosettaVS, TerraBind)
gaps: Size mismatch between biologically relevant systems and NISQ quantum hardware capacity
Heuristic search provides no optimality guarantees
Scoring functions lack accuracy for entropy and induced-fit effects
DL methods show poor generalization to novel binding pockets

top_np_hard_problems.problem: Protein Sidechain Packing (Rotamer Assignment)
top_np_hard_problems.complexity: NP-hard — selecting one rotamer per residue from a discrete library to minimize total pairwise-decomposable conformational energy is provably intractable (Pierce & Winfree, 2002)
current_approaches: Dead-end elimination (DEE)
Integer linear programming
Monte Carlo stochastic search (Rosetta packer)
Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA) with QUBO encoding
AlphaFold2 backbone prediction + refinement
gaps: AlphaFold2 sidechain positioning deviates from experimental data by up to 20%
Rosetta packer is heuristic with no global optimality guarantee
QAOA shot scaling remains below classical exhaustive search rates at moderate flexibility
Classical preprocessing does not significantly reduce low-energy basins

top_np_hard_problems.problem: Protein Structure Alignment (Optimal RMSD under Correspondence)
top_np_hard_problems.complexity: NP-hard — reducible to the largest common point set (LCP) problem or 3D substructure isomorphism, both proven NP-complete (Goldman et al., 1999)
current_approaches: Dynamic programming (CE, Dali)
Spectral methods (GESAMT)
Heuristic search (TM-align)
Contact map overlap maximization
gaps: Exhaustive search is O(n!·m!) for proteins of length n, m
Continuous 6-DOF search space cannot be discretely sampled without missing global optimum
Scoring functions are non-convex with many local minima
Flexible alignment with rotamers is NP-complete to NP-hard

top_np_hard_problems.problem: Protein Threading (3D Fold Recognition)
top_np_hard_problems.complexity: NP-complete for detailed models (Lathrop, 1994) — aligning sequence to structural template with pairwise interactions is intractable
current_approaches: Dynamic programming over frozen environments
Graph-based algorithms
Deep learning fold recognition
gaps: Simplified models required for tractability
Energy function accuracy degrades with sequence length
Cannot guarantee optimal fold assignment

top_np_hard_problems.problem: Flexible Ligand-Flexible Receptor Docking
top_np_hard_problems.complexity: NP-hard — even simplified models with both ligand and receptor flexibility are intractable (Fraenkel, 1993)
current_approaches: FFT correlation methods
Monte Carlo simulation
Genetic algorithms
Incremental construction (DOCK, FlexX)
gaps: Induced-fit effects poorly captured by rigid-receptor approximations
Ensemble docking multiplies computational cost
No polynomial-time algorithm exists for guaranteed optimal solution

top_np_hard_problems.problem: IoT Medical Device Scheduling and Resource Allocation (RCSP variant)
top_np_hard_problems.complexity: NP-hard (bi-objective variant of Resource-Constrained Scheduling Problem with time windows, device compatibility, battery limits, and setup times)
current_approaches: NSGA-II genetic algorithm for bi-objective optimization of cost vs quality of care
Grey Wolf Optimisation (GWO) with BRAD-GWA for multi-scenario bimetric-balanced allocation
Genetic Simulated Annealing Algorithm (GSAA) for energy-efficient containerized resource allocation
gaps: No polynomial-time exact solution exists; all approaches are meta-heuristic approximations
Dynamic patient admission/discharge patterns make static schedules obsolete within hours
Multi-objective Pareto front computation scales exponentially with device and patient count

top_np_hard_problems.problem: Multi-Resource Constrained Elective Surgical Scheduling (MESS)
top_np_hard_problems.complexity: NP-hard combinatorial optimization (multi-player game with material resources like ORs/NOR beds and human resources like surgeons/anesthesiologists/nurses)
current_approaches: Nash equilibrium-based game-theoretic allocation across three player types
Digital twin-based simulation for surgical scheduling optimization
Meta-heuristic algorithms for multi-objective optimization (APT, AOT, TC)
gaps: Uncertain surgery durations make deterministic scheduling impossible
Nash equilibrium computation is PPAD-complete in general games
Integration with real-time IoT device availability data remains unsolved

top_np_hard_problems.problem: Joint Task Partitioning and Parallel Scheduling in Device-Assisted Mobile Edge Networks
top_np_hard_problems.complexity: NP-hard (reduces to multiple knapsack problem; non-linear integer programming formulation)
current_approaches: Fair and Delay-Minimized Task Scheduling (FDMTS) algorithm
Device-assisted computation offloading with idle resource differentiation
Heuristic partitioning with greedy result allocation
gaps: Time-varying system state (channel conditions, device mobility) invalidates static partitions
Fairness vs delay minimization trade-off lacks closed-form optimal solution
Scalability to thousands of concurrent IoT devices unproven

top_np_hard_problems.problem: Fog/Edge Module Placement and Data Placement (Generalized Assignment Problem)
top_np_hard_problems.complexity: NP-hard (formulated as Generalized Assignment Problem with latency, energy, and cost constraints)
current_approaches: Integer programming exact solutions for small instances
Geographical zoning heuristics for large fog node counts (iFogStor)
ML-based rate-adaptive frameworks (ML-RASPF) for dynamic resource allocation
gaps: Exact integer programming does not scale beyond tens of fog nodes
Data placement decisions are coupled with computation placement, creating interdependent NP-hard subproblems
Patient mobility patterns in hospital environments create non-stationary placement requirements

top_np_hard_problems.problem: Multi-Objective Task Offloading and Scheduling in Edge-Cloud Continuum
top_np_hard_problems.complexity: NP-hard (joint optimization of energy consumption, latency, and deadline meeting rate across heterogeneous edge/fog/cloud tiers)
current_approaches: MOSAIC: Mobility-Oriented Scheduling with Levy Walk/Random Walk mobility models
Q-learning with epsilon-greedy policy for Markov decision model of patient-resource matching
Particle swarm optimization for cloud-based IoT task scheduling
gaps: Q-table size grows exponentially with problem scale, making convergence difficult
Hard real-time task guarantees cannot be probabilistically assured
Co-optimization of energy, latency, and deadline adherence lacks unified framework

top_np_hard_problems.problem: Minimum-Cost Set Cover for Clinical Trial Site Selection: Selecting the minimum-cost set of investigative sites that collectively cover all required patient subpopulations, geographic regions, and enrollment targets. This is a generalization of the NP-hard Set Cover problem (Karp 1972).
top_np_hard_problems.complexity: NP-hard; greedy approximation achieves H(n) ≈ ln(n)+1 ratio, which is optimal unless P=NP (Feige 1998)
current_approaches: Greedy set cover heuristics with cost-effectiveness scoring
Integer linear programming (ILP) for exact solutions on small instances
Genetic algorithms for multi-objective optimization (accuracy, fairness, competition)
DocTr: cross-modal deep learning with genetic algorithm optimization for clinician-trial matching (Gao et al. 2026, Nature Health)
gaps: No polynomial-time algorithm can beat ln(n) approximation unless P=NP
Multi-objective fairness constraints (racial, ethnic, geographic diversity) make the problem harder
Dynamic enrollment rates and site capacity constraints are not well-modeled

top_np_hard_problems.problem: Patient-Trial Matching as Bipartite Graph Assignment: Matching patients to trials where each patient may be eligible for multiple trials and each trial has multiple slots, with the objective of maximizing total enrollment while respecting eligibility constraints. This is a generalization of the Assignment Problem with additional constraints.
top_np_hard_problems.complexity: NP-hard when extended to many-to-many matching with eligibility constraints; basic assignment is polynomial (Hungarian algorithm O(n³)) but constrained versions are NP-hard
current_approaches: DeepEnroll: cross-modal deep embedding with entailment prediction (Zhang et al. 2020)
TrialGPT: LLM-based matching with criterion-level evaluation (Jin et al. 2024, Nature Communications)
COMPOSE: embedding-based patient-trial matching (Gao et al. 2020)
TrialMatchAI: RAG-based hybrid search with criterion-level eligibility assessment (Abdallah et al. 2025)
SMT-based matching: Satisfiability Modulo Theories for logical reasoning over eligibility criteria (Stanford LAM)
gaps: O(n²) pairwise matching complexity does not scale to millions of patients × 500K trials
LLM-based approaches struggle with temporal logic, derived clinical variables, and numeric thresholds
Generalizability across disease areas and institutions remains limited
No approach guarantees 100% recall with high precision at scale

top_np_hard_problems.problem: Set Balancing for Stratified Randomization: Partitioning patients into treatment arms such that all arms have nearly identical distributions of covariates (age, sex, biomarkers, disease severity) while differing only in treatment assignment. This is the NP-hard Set Balancing problem.
top_np_hard_problems.complexity: NP-hard; no known polynomial-time exact algorithm; approximation algorithms and heuristics required
current_approaches: Stratified permuted block randomization
Minimization methods (Pocock & Simon)
Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA) and Quantum Walk Optimization (QWOA) for QUBO formulations (arXiv:2509.07200)
Shannon-entropy-based post-processing for feature-distribution uniformity
gaps: High-dimensional covariate spaces make exact balancing infeasible
No constant-factor approximation known for general case
Dynamic/adaptive balancing during trial enrollment adds further complexity

top_np_hard_problems.problem: Combinatorial Optimization for Eligibility Criteria Design: Selecting the optimal set of eligibility criteria that maximizes eligible patient pool while maintaining scientific validity and statistical power. Each criterion eliminates a multiplicative fraction of candidates.
top_np_hard_problems.complexity: NP-hard; equivalent to a constrained optimization over combinatorial space of criteria combinations
current_approaches: NLP-based simulation of eligible patient counts under different criteria combinations (Sharma et al. 2024, JMIR)
Knowledge-base-driven criteria optimization using real-world EHR data
FDA 2022 guidance on eligibility broadening
gaps: Criteria interactions are multiplicative and non-linear, making optimization difficult
Trade-off between internal validity (strict criteria) and external validity (broad criteria) is not formally optimized
Rare disease trials face extreme combinatorial explosion of biomarker combinations

top_np_hard_problems.problem: Multipartite entity resolution (patient record linkage across multiple databases)
top_np_hard_problems.complexity: NP-hard — formulated as the Multidimensional Assignment Problem (MAP); brute-force comparison is O(n²) requiring (n²-n)/2 comparisons
current_approaches: Blocking techniques (sorted neighborhood, bigram indexing, canopy generation) to reduce comparison space from O(n²) to O(n·b)
Fellegi-Sunter probabilistic model with EM algorithm for weight computation
Greedy and Very Large Scale Neighborhood Search (VLNS) heuristics for MAP
Hybrid contrastive learning + deterministic rules with clique cover clustering
Bloom filter-based privacy-preserving record linkage
gaps: No polynomial-time exact solution exists for multipartite case
Optimal clique cover is NP-hard; greedy heuristics used in practice
Missing and erroneous QID values degrade linkage quality
Scalability beyond 300K records requires aggressive blocking that loses recall

top_np_hard_problems.problem: Ontology matching and semantic alignment between heterogeneous terminologies (SNOMED CT, ICD-10, LOINC, RxNorm, CPT, NDC)
top_np_hard_problems.complexity: NP-hard — correlation clustering formulation; subquadratic approximation required for practical use
current_approaches: Expert-curated reference sets for direct 1-to-1 mappings
Logistic regression-based imputation with medBERT text embeddings (AUC 0.95+ for NDC, 0.85 for CPT)
Patient-context-aware ranking using SNOMED CT hierarchical structure (Node2Vec, shortest-path, cosine similarity)
Two-step LLM-based alignment pipeline with candidate generation and acceptance/rejection
UMLS Metathesaurus as cross-terminology mapping backbone
gaps: Full automation remains an open problem requiring advances in ontology alignment and ML-driven entity resolution
Multiple regional versions of SNOMED CT and ICD-10 coexist with frequent updates
No gold standard mappings exist for CPT and NDC to SNOMED CT
Context-dependent mappings (one LOINC to multiple SNOMED CT codes) resist 1-to-1 automation

top_np_hard_problems.problem: Schema matching and data harmonization across heterogeneous EHR formats
top_np_hard_problems.complexity: NP-hard — correlation clustering is NP-hard (Filkov and Skiena 2003; Bansal et al. 2004); pairwise schema matching scales as O(N²) in number of schemas
current_approaches: Ontology-based mediation with vector-space embeddings for candidate generation
LLM-based accept/reject classification for candidate pairs
OMOP CDM as common target model with ETL transformation pipelines
FHIR StructureMap and ConceptMap for declarative transformations
AQL (Archetype Query Language) for openEHR-to-OMOP conversion via Eos/OMOCL
gaps: No universal automated harmonization solution exists
Institution-specific data collection standards and infrastructure differences persist
Medical knowledge evolves continuously making static mappings obsolete
Full interoperability requires advances in ontology alignment, ML-driven entity resolution, and expert validation simultaneously

top_np_hard_problems.problem: Optimal feature selection in high-dimensional omics data
top_np_hard_problems.complexity: NP-hard: search space includes 2^n - 1 feature subsets for n features; no polynomial-time algorithm achieves minimax-optimal recovery under worst-case designs
current_approaches: Filter methods (t-test, ANOVA, Wilcoxon, mutual information, MRMR)
Wrapper methods with metaheuristic optimization (SPHMO, genetic algorithms)
Embedded methods (LASSO, elastic net, tree-based importance)
Hybrid filter-plus-elimination (FLASH, MAFS with multi-head attention)
Quantum-inspired QUBO formulations for gene selection
gaps: No polynomial-time algorithm achieves information-theoretic optimal sample complexity
Heuristic methods yield inconsistent performance across datasets
Statistical-computational trade-off: efficient algorithms require stronger design conditions (restricted eigenvalues, incoherence)
Scalability limited to feature spaces of ~18,000 features in practice

top_np_hard_problems.problem: Best subset selection for multi-omics biomarker discovery
top_np_hard_problems.complexity: NP-hard: statistically minimax optimal but computationally intractable; exponential in the number of features
current_approaches: Convex relaxation (Lasso, sparse PCA)
Graphlet screening for sparse Gram matrices
AdaSub / local search with polynomial adaptivity
Two-stage ETS framework with polylog time per estimate
gaps: Efficient algorithms incur additional sample complexity cost inversely proportional to squared restricted eigenvalue
No method simultaneously achieves minimax statistical optimality and polynomial computational complexity
Multi-omics extension of best subset selection remains largely unexplored

top_np_hard_problems.problem: Network alignment and matching across omics layers
top_np_hard_problems.complexity: NP-hard: subgraph isomorphism and graph matching problems; exact alignment of multi-layer networks is computationally infeasible at scale
current_approaches: Graph-linked unified embedding (GLUE) with guidance graphs
Anchor-based integration (Seurat CCA/RPCA)
Manifold alignment (Pamona)
Non-negative matrix factorization (LIGER iNMF)
gaps: Scalable exact alignment remains elusive for atlas-scale datasets
Prior knowledge graphs may be incomplete or biased
Unpaired data integration requires approximate matching with quality guarantees

top_np_hard_problems.problem: Multi-objective optimization for omics layer selection and integration strategy
top_np_hard_problems.complexity: NP-hard: selecting optimal omics layers and integration architecture involves combinatorial optimization over 2^k possible layer combinations and multiple competing objectives
current_approaches: Unsupervised factor analysis (MOFA+) for automatic relevance determination
Supervised latent variable approaches (DIABLO)
Network-based integration with modularity optimization
gaps: No principled method for determining which omics layers to include a priori
Integration strategy selection (early/intermediate/late) remains largely heuristic
Trade-offs between interpretability and predictive performance not formally characterized

top_np_hard_problems.problem: Nurse Rostering Problem (NRP) / Nurse Scheduling Problem (NSP)
top_np_hard_problems.complexity: NP-hard; proven strongly NP-hard even with only three work shifts and one day-off shift; exact solutions feasible only for small instances
current_approaches: Mixed Integer Linear Programming (MILP) with branch-and-price for small instances
Constraint Programming (CP-SAT) enforcing 14 hard constraints with 15 soft objectives
Metaheuristics: genetic algorithms, simulated annealing, variable neighborhood search, bat algorithms
Multi-objective NSGA-II for Pareto-optimal trade-offs between cost, coverage, and satisfaction
gaps: Cannot guarantee regulatory compliance at scale
Lack real-time adaptability to staff shortages or emergency priorities
Multi-role, multi-skill workforce heterogeneity poorly modeled
Inter-week schedule stability and cross-midnight shift patterns remain challenging

top_np_hard_problems.problem: Medical Appointment Scheduling with Clinical Constraints
top_np_hard_problems.complexity: NP-hard; generalizes to constrained assignment problems with temporal, resource, and preference constraints
current_approaches: Answer Set Programming (ASP) for declarative constraint solving with <0.04s solve times
Genetic Algorithms achieving 100% constraint fulfillment vs 60-40% for FCFS baselines
First-Come-First-Served (FCFS) and Random Choice as deterministic baselines
gaps: Centralized reservation systems (e.g., Italy's CUP) assign appointments without considering medical urgency, patient location, or preferences
High no-show rates and administrative overhead from manual rescheduling
Rigid frameworks cannot handle real-time variations in staff shortages or emergency priorities

top_np_hard_problems.problem: Home Healthcare Routing and Scheduling (bi-objective VRPTW)
top_np_hard_problems.complexity: NP-hard; formulated as Vehicle Routing Problem with Time Windows (VRPTWs); optimal solutions very hard to obtain in practice
current_approaches: Mixed Integer Linear Programming with bi-objective function
Simulated Annealing with weighted sum approach and local search operators (swapping, moving, path exchange, ruin and recreate)
Pareto front exploration via multi-objective metaheuristics
gaps: Multi-objective nature requires balancing travel cost vs workload equity
Customized optimization techniques needed for each healthcare setting
Scalability to large patient populations remains limited

top_np_hard_problems.problem: Multi-Objective Healthcare Workforce Scheduling
top_np_hard_problems.complexity: NP-hard combinatorial optimization; computational cost grows exponentially with problem size
current_approaches: NSGA-II for Pareto front generation across operational efficiency, patient care quality, and staff satisfaction
Three-phase modified bat algorithms for shift schedule generation and correction
Multi-Neighborhood Simulated Annealing (MNSA) for integrated timetabling
gaps: Exact methods impractical for large-scale dynamic hospital scheduling
Acuity-weighted workload equity across employees not well addressed
Sub-shift temporal granularity (15-minute resolution) increases model size near-linearly at ~4,400 variables per employee

top_np_hard_problems.problem: Patient-to-Room and Nurse-to-Patient Integrated Assignment
top_np_hard_problems.complexity: NP-hard; joint assignment of multiple resource types with interdependent constraints
current_approaches: Integrated Healthcare Timetabling Competition formulations
Multi-Neighborhood Simulated Annealing with tailored neighborhood operators
Constraint programming with hard/soft constraint separation
gaps: Integrated problems combining multiple resource types remain computationally intractable at scale
Real-time reallocation under disruptions (emergencies, no-shows) poorly handled
